## claude.ai Datadog
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. ===== ISSUE #438 =====
Docs: sync the crate table in CLAUDE.md to all 91 workspace members
LABELS: documentation,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
The workspace has **91 members** (verified: `Cargo.toml` `[workspace].members`), and CLAUDE.md's intro says "91 crates", but the crate table lists only ~78 `| faucet-* |` rows. Whole connector families are missing from the table: **azure-blob** (source+sink), **pubsub** (source+sink+common), **clickhouse** (source+sink+common), and **redshift** (source+sink+common).

## Motivation
CLAUDE.md's own "Keeping This File Up to Date" section makes the crate table the single source of truth for the workspace. A table that omits shipped connectors misleads every future contributor (and Claude session) about what exists. Pure docs, fully verifiable, zero code risk.

## Proposed change
- `CLAUDE.md` — add the missing rows to the crate table (mirroring the existing one-line-description style), covering at minimum: `faucet-source-azure-blob`, `faucet-sink-azure-blob`, `faucet-source-pubsub`, `faucet-sink-pubsub`, `faucet-common-pubsub`, `faucet-source-clickhouse`, `faucet-sink-clickhouse`, `faucet-common-clickhouse`, `faucet-source-redshift`, `faucet-sink-redshift`, `faucet-common-redshift`. Cross-check the full row set against `Cargo.toml` members so the table row count matches 91.
- While here, verify the root `README.md` connector counts/table reflect the same set (update if stale).

## Affected crates / files
- `CLAUDE.md` (crate table), and `README.md` connector table/counts if they disagree.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every workspace member in `Cargo.toml` has a corresponding crate-table row in CLAUDE.md.
- Descriptions follow the existing terse one-line style.
- README connector table/counts match (or a note explains any intentional difference).

## Out of scope
- Any code change; this is documentation only.


===== ISSUE #437 =====
Refactor+test: extract a pure `progress_ratio` in backfill metrics
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`cli/src/backfill/metrics.rs::set_progress` (~L43) computes a completion ratio inline (`if planned == 0 { 1.0 } else { done / planned }`) and immediately feeds it to a `metrics` gauge macro, so the divide-by-zero guard and clamping can't be unit-tested. Extract the arithmetic into a tiny pure fn and test it.

## Motivation
The `0/0`, `done < planned`, and `done == planned` cases are exactly where a progress bar goes wrong (NaN, >1.0). A pure `progress_ratio(done, planned) -> f64` makes them testable without touching the metrics recorder.

## Proposed change
- `cli/src/backfill/metrics.rs` — pull the ratio logic into `fn progress_ratio(done: usize, planned: usize) -> f64`, call it from `set_progress`, and add a `#[cfg(test)]` module covering: `planned == 0` → `1.0`; `done == 0, planned > 0` → `0.0`; `done == planned` → `1.0`; `done < planned` → the expected fraction; (optionally) `done > planned` clamped to `1.0`.

## Affected crates / files
- `cli/src/backfill/metrics.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- `progress_ratio` exists as a pure fn and is used by `set_progress`.
- Tests cover the four/five cases above and never produce NaN.
- `cargo test -p faucet-cli` passes.

## Out of scope
- Changing what metric is emitted or its name.


===== ISSUE #436 =====
Tests: cover `RunStreamOptions` builder methods
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`crates/core/src/observability/options.rs` defines the `RunStreamOptions` builder (`with_name`, `with_row`, `with_run_id`, `with_state`, `with_dlq`, `with_cancel`, `with_adaptive`, `with_quality`, …) but has no `#[cfg(test)]` module and isn't exercised by `crates/core/tests/*`.

## Motivation
These builders are pure and directly shape pipeline behavior (bookmarks, DLQ, delivery, cancellation). A small test that each `with_*` sets exactly its field and that chaining composes protects a widely-used public API with almost no effort — an ideal first contribution.

## Proposed change
- `crates/core/src/observability/options.rs` — add a `#[cfg(test)]` module asserting that each `with_*` populates the corresponding `Option`/field, leaves the others at default, and that a chained builder composes all set fields.

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/core/src/observability/options.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- Each builder method has at least one assertion.
- A chaining test sets several fields and verifies all are retained.
- `cargo test -p faucet-core` passes.

## Out of scope
- Testing the streaming loop that consumes the options.


===== ISSUE #435 =====
Tests: broaden `glob_match` edge-case coverage (SFTP source)
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`crates/source/sftp/src/config.rs` has a hand-rolled backtracking `glob_match` (~L93) used to filter remote listings. Its test module (~L188) covers `*` / `?` / literals / multi-star, but not the off-by-one boundary cases a backtracking matcher classically gets wrong.

## Motivation
Glob matching decides which remote files a run ingests; a subtle boundary bug means silently skipping or over-including files. The missing cases are exactly the ones worth pinning.

## Proposed change
- `crates/source/sftp/src/config.rs` — add cases to the existing `#[cfg(test)]` module, e.g.:
  - `glob_match("", "")` → `true`
  - `glob_match("", "x")` → `false`
  - `glob_match("a?", "a")` → `false` (trailing `?` with exhausted input)
  - `glob_match("abc", "ab")` → `false` (pattern longer than name, no star)
  - `glob_match("*", "")` → `true`
  - `glob_match("a*", "a")` → `true`

Fix `glob_match` only if one of these reveals an actual bug; otherwise this is a pure test-hardening change.

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/source/sftp/src/config.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- The new assertions are added and pass (or a real bug is fixed to make them pass).
- `cargo test -p faucet-source-sftp` passes.

## Out of scope
- Replacing the matcher with a glob crate.


===== ISSUE #434 =====
Tests: cover `faucet init` `resolve_kinds` / `unknown_kind_err`
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`cli/src/commands/init.rs` has no `#[cfg(test)]` module. `resolve_kinds` (~L180) maps CLI args → `(source_kind, sink_kind)` via in-memory registry lookups (no I/O) and errors through `unknown_kind_err` (~L300) on an unknown kind. Both are easily unit-testable in the non-interactive path.

## Motivation
`init` is the primary onboarding command; its arg-resolution logic is pure and should be pinned by tests so registry/label changes don't regress the error path or the defaults.

## Proposed change
- `cli/src/commands/init.rs` — add a `#[cfg(test)]` module testing `resolve_kinds`:
  - valid `--source`/`--sink` kinds pass through unchanged;
  - omitted args fall back to the documented defaults;
  - an unknown source or sink kind returns the expected `CliError` (via `unknown_kind_err`).

## Affected crates / files
- `cli/src/commands/init.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- Tests cover the valid, default, and unknown-kind cases.
- `cargo test -p faucet-cli` passes.

## Out of scope
- The `cli-interactive` (`inquire`) TTY path.


===== ISSUE #433 =====
Tests: add unit test for `is_topology()` predicate
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`cli/src/topology.rs` has no `#[cfg(test)]` module, yet `is_topology(cfg)` (~L27) is the load-bearing predicate that branches `run`/`validate`/`preview` between matrix mode and topology mode. It is trivially pure (`!cfg.pipeline.nodes.is_empty()`) — a perfect first test.

## Motivation
A one-line predicate that decides a major execution branch deserves a regression test so a future refactor of `PipelineSpec` can't silently flip the branch.

## Proposed change
- `cli/src/topology.rs` — add a `#[cfg(test)]` module that builds a minimal `PipelineConfig` (parse a tiny YAML/JSON via `PipelineConfig::from_text`) with and without a `pipeline.nodes` block and asserts `is_topology` returns `true` / `false` respectively.

## Affected crates / files
- `cli/src/topology.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- Two cases: non-empty `pipeline.nodes` → `true`; absent/empty → `false`.
- `cargo test -p faucet-cli` passes.

## Out of scope
- Testing the full topology builder/executor.


===== ISSUE #432 =====
CLI: `faucet schema --list` to enumerate valid schema targets
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`faucet schema <target>` supports many targets (`config`, `source`, `sink`, `transform`, `dlq`, `replication`, `backfill`, `execution`, `resilience`, `sla`, …) but there is no way to discover the valid set from the CLI. A mistyped target yields a hard error with no list. Add `faucet schema --list` that prints the available targets.

## Motivation
Discoverability: users shouldn't have to read the source or the docs to learn which schema targets exist. This mirrors the self-describing spirit of `faucet list`.

## Proposed change
- `cli/src/cli.rs` — add `#[arg(long)] pub list: bool` to `SchemaArgs` (~L1011); make the positional target optional when `--list` is passed.
- `cli/src/commands/schema.rs` — when `list` is set, print the target names (the `SchemaTarget` variants dispatched at ~L11-40) and return before dispatching.

## Affected crates / files
- `cli/src/cli.rs`, `cli/src/commands/schema.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- `faucet schema --list` prints every valid target name and exits 0.
- Existing `faucet schema <target>` behavior is unchanged.
- A test asserts the listing includes known targets (e.g. `source`, `sink`, `dlq`).
- `docs/book/src/reference/cli.md` mentions `--list`.

## Out of scope
- Listing individual connector/transform names (that is `faucet list`).


===== ISSUE #431 =====
Kafka sink: make Schema Registry encode errors actionable
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
When a Confluent Schema-Registry value format is selected on the Kafka sink but no Schema Registry client was built, encoding fails with a terse message that states the problem but not the fix.

## Motivation
`FaucetError::Config("ConfluentAvro selected but no SchemaRegistryClient")` (and the Protobuf / JsonSchema twins) tell the user *what* is wrong but not *how* to fix it. A one-line hint naming the missing config field turns a head-scratcher into a self-service fix.

## Proposed change
- `crates/sink/kafka/src/encode.rs` — extend the three error strings at ~L47 (Avro), ~L58 (Protobuf), ~L69 (JsonSchema) to point at the fix, e.g.:
  `"value format 'confluent_avro' requires a Schema Registry client — set `schema_registry.url` (and any auth) in the Kafka sink config"`.

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/sink/kafka/src/encode.rs` (three sites).

## Acceptance criteria
- All three messages name the missing config (`schema_registry.url`) and the selected format.
- A unit test asserts the improved message text for at least one format.
- No behavior change beyond the message.

## Out of scope
- Any change to how the Schema Registry client is constructed.


===== ISSUE #430 =====
Validation: S3 / GCS sink configs accept an empty `bucket`
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
The object-store sink configs require a `bucket` name but never reject an empty string. An empty `bucket` should be a load-time config error, not a runtime API failure.

## Motivation
Fail-fast validation: a blank `bucket` (typo, unset `${env:...}`) currently sails through config load and only blows up when the first upload hits the cloud API with an opaque error. A typed `FaucetError::Config` at load time is far clearer.

## Proposed change
- `crates/sink/s3/src/config.rs` — `bucket` at ~L28. Add `pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), faucet_core::FaucetError>` that returns `FaucetError::Config` when `bucket` is empty (also call `validate_batch_size` if the config carries one), and invoke it at construction.
- `crates/sink/gcs/src/config.rs` — `bucket` at ~L29. Same treatment.

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/sink/s3/src/config.rs`, `crates/sink/gcs/src/config.rs` (+ construction sites).

## Acceptance criteria
- Building either sink with an empty `bucket` returns a typed `FaucetError::Config` naming the field.
- Valid configs are unaffected.
- Unit tests cover empty-`bucket` rejection and a valid config passing.

## Out of scope
- Source-side validation (tracked in the source-config `validate()` issue).


===== ISSUE #428 =====
CLI: add `--json` output to `faucet validate`
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`faucet validate` is a CI-oriented command but only emits prose (`ok: '...' rows=...`, per-row role lines). Add a `--json` flag that prints a structured validation summary so CI systems can assert on it programmatically.

## Motivation
Teams gate merges on `faucet validate`. Parsing prose is brittle; a stable JSON summary (config name, row count, per-row source/sink/roles, run/skip selection decision) makes the command reliable in automation and consistent with the `--json` flags already on `list`/`search`/`conformance`.

## Proposed change
- `cli/src/cli.rs` — add `#[arg(long)] pub json: bool` to `ValidateArgs` (~L978).
- `cli/src/commands/validate.rs` — the human path (`run`, ~L17; `println!` lines ~L56-64 and ~L147-206) already computes per-row data. Collect it into a `#[derive(Serialize)]` summary struct and emit it with `serde_json::to_string_pretty` when `--json` is set.

## Affected crates / files
- `cli/src/cli.rs`, `cli/src/commands/validate.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- `faucet validate <cfg> --json` prints a JSON object with at least: config `name`, `row_count`, and a `rows` array (each with `id`, `source`, `sink`, role/parent info, and the RUN/skip decision when a selector is active).
- Non-`--json` output is unchanged.
- A test validates a known example config with `--json` and asserts the parsed shape.
- `docs/book/src/reference/cli.md` documents the flag.

## Out of scope
- Changing validation logic or the human-readable report.


===== ISSUE #427 =====
CLI: add `--json` output to `faucet list`
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`faucet list` only prints human-readable columns via `println!`. Sibling commands already expose a machine-readable `--json` flag (`faucet search`, `faucet conformance`), so this is a small consistency/ergonomics gap. Add `--json` so the compiled-in sources/sinks/transforms/state-stores (and the `--available` registry rows) can be consumed by tooling and CI.

## Motivation
Users scripting around faucet (dashboards, CI checks, editor integrations) currently have to scrape the printed table. A JSON mode makes `list` composable and consistent with the rest of the CLI surface.

## Proposed change
- `cli/src/cli.rs` — add `#[arg(long)] pub json: bool` to `ListArgs` (~L1227). For reference, `ConformanceArgs.json` (~L1251) and `SearchArgs.json` (~L1268) already do this.
- `cli/src/commands/list.rs` — in `run` (~L17) and `list_available` (~L44), when `json` is set, serialize the collected data to a JSON object (arrays of `{name, description, tier}` for sources/sinks, names for transforms/state-stores) with `serde_json::to_string_pretty` instead of the printed columns.

## Affected crates / files
- `cli/src/cli.rs`, `cli/src/commands/list.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- `faucet list --json` emits valid JSON covering sources, sinks, transforms, and state stores.
- `faucet list --available --json` emits the registry-index rows as JSON.
- Existing human output is unchanged when `--json` is absent.
- A unit/integration test asserts the JSON shape parses and contains a known built-in (e.g. `rest`, `jsonl`).

===== ISSUE #437 =====
Refactor+test: extract a pure `progress_ratio` in backfill metrics
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`cli/src/backfill/metrics.rs::set_progress` (~L43) computes a completion ratio inline (`if planned == 0 { 1.0 } else { done / planned }`) and immediately feeds it to a `metrics` gauge macro, so the divide-by-zero guard and clamping can't be unit-tested. Extract the arithmetic into a tiny pure fn and test it.

## Motivation
The `0/0`, `done < planned`, and `done == planned` cases are exactly where a progress bar goes wrong (NaN, >1.0). A pure `progress_ratio(done, planned) -> f64` makes them testable without touching the metrics recorder.

## Proposed change
- `cli/src/backfill/metrics.rs` — pull the ratio logic into `fn progress_ratio(done: usize, planned: usize) -> f64`, call it from `set_progress`, and add a `#[cfg(test)]` module covering: `planned == 0` → `1.0`; `done == 0, planned > 0` → `0.0`; `done == planned` → `1.0`; `done < planned` → the expected fraction; (optionally) `done > planned` clamped to `1.0`.

## Affected crates / files
- `cli/src/backfill/metrics.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- `progress_ratio` exists as a pure fn and is used by `set_progress`.
- Tests cover the four/five cases above and never produce NaN.
- `cargo test -p faucet-cli` passes.

- Changing what metric is emitted or its name.

===== ISSUE #435 =====
Tests: broaden `glob_match` edge-case coverage (SFTP source)
LABELS: enhancement,good first issue,tier-3
---
## Summary
`crates/source/sftp/src/config.rs` has a hand-rolled backtracking `glob_match` (~L93) used to filter remote listings. Its test module (~L188) covers `*` / `?` / literals / multi-star, but not the off-by-one boundary cases a backtracking matcher classically gets wrong.

Glob matching decides which remote files a run ingests; a subtle boundary bug means silently skipping or over-including files. The missing cases are exactly the ones worth pinning.

- `crates/source/sftp/src/config.rs` — add cases to the existing `#[cfg(test)]` module, e.g.:

  - `glob_match("", "x")` → `false`
  - `glob_match("a?", "a")` → `false` (trailing `?` with exhausted input)
  - `glob_match("abc", "ab")` → `false` (pattern longer than name, no star)
  - `glob_match("*", "")` → `true`
  - `glob_match("a*", "a")` → `true`

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/source/sftp/src/config.rs`

- The new assertions are added and pass (or a real bug is fixed to make them pass).

- Replacing the matcher with a glob crate.

88	confirmation line per reference (never the value):
89	
90	```
91	secret: vault:secret/data/faucet/api#token → resolved
92	ok: 'my-pipeline' rows=1 (roots=1, children=0) execution=(defaults)
93	  - default [root] source=rest sink=jsonl delivery=at-least-once
94	```
95	
96	Each row line ends with the **derived end-to-end delivery guarantee** for that
97	row's source × sink × config — `at-least-once`,
98	`effectively-once (atomic watermark)`, or `effectively-once (keyed upsert)` —
99	computed regardless of the requested `delivery:` mode, so an upsert-keyed row
100	is reported as effectively-once even without `delivery: exactly_once`. See
101	[`delivery`](./config.md#delivery).
102	
103	Pass `--no-secrets` to validate grammar and structure only, skipping all secret
104	fetches. This is useful in CI environments that lack credentials, or in local
105	development before vault access is available:

109	```

112	validates against **type-shaped placeholders** for any `required` param, so a
113	parameterized config passes CI without inventing values:

## `validate`

Reports one line per expanded matrix row. Use it in CI to catch config errors
before deploying.

```bash
faucet validate pipeline.yaml
```

When the config contains secrets-manager directives (`${vault:…}`, `${aws-sm:…}`,
etc.), `faucet validate` resolves them as a real preflight and prints one
confirmation line per reference (never the value):

```
secret: vault:secret/data/faucet/api#token → resolved
ok: 'my-pipeline' rows=1 (roots=1, children=0) execution=(defaults)
  - default [root] source=rest sink=jsonl delivery=at-least-once
```

Each row line ends with the **derived end-to-end delivery guarantee** for that
row's source × sink × config — `at-least-once`,
`effectively-once (atomic watermark)`, or `effectively-once (keyed upsert)` —
computed regardless of the requested `delivery:` mode, so an upsert-keyed row
is reported as effectively-once even without `delivery: exactly_once`. See
[`delivery`](./config.md#delivery).

Pass `--no-secrets` to validate grammar and structure only, skipping all secret
fetches. This is useful in CI environments that lack credentials, or in local
development before vault access is available:


## `search` / `install` / `list --available`

Discover connectors from the [connector registry](../extending/marketplace.md) —
a curated, feature-independent index of every built-in connector plus community
`faucet-source-*` / `faucet-sink-*` crates.

```bash
faucet search kafka              # matches on name, description, keywords, crate
faucet search cdc --json         # machine-readable
faucet list --available          # the whole registry; ● = in this binary, ○ = installable
faucet install bigquery --kind sink
faucet install my-connector --index ./my-registry.json
```

`faucet install <name>` never runs anything — it prints the recipe:

- a **built-in** already compiled in → "already available";
- a **built-in** not compiled in → `cargo install faucet-cli --features <kind>-<name>`;
- a **community** connector → a copy-pasteable custom-binary snippet (see
  [Custom binaries](../../cli/README.md#custom-binaries-with-third-party-connectors)).

`--index <path>` points any of these at a custom/mirror index instead of the
built-in one. Ambiguous names (a connector that is both a source and a sink,
e.g. `postgres`) need `--kind source|sink`.

# MongoDB collection → local Parquet files.
#
# Streams documents out of a MongoDB collection (with a filter, projection, and
# sort) and writes them as columnar Parquet — the Arrow schema is inferred from
# the first batch of records, so no schema declaration is needed. Ideal for
# snapshotting an operational collection into an analytics-friendly file format.
#
# Infra: MongoDB from `examples/docker-compose.yml` (the `mongodb` service).
# The Parquet sink writes to the local filesystem — no cloud credentials needed.
#
# Run:
#   docker compose -f examples/docker-compose.yml up -d mongodb
#   faucet validate cli/examples/mongodb_to_parquet.yaml
#   faucet run      cli/examples/mongodb_to_parquet.yaml
version: 1
name: mongodb_to_parquet

pipeline:
  source:
    type: mongodb
    config:
      # Standard MongoDB connection string. Point at your replica set / cluster.
      connection_uri: mongodb://localhost:27017
      database: shop
      collection: orders
      # Server-side filter — only completed orders are exported.
      filter:
        status: completed
      # Return just the fields we care about (1 = include). Drop `_id` so the
      # ObjectId doesn't need type handling downstream.
      projection:
        _id: 0
        customer_id: 1
        total: 1
        currency: 1
        created_at: 1
      # Deterministic ordering makes re-runs reproducible.
      sort:
        created_at: 1
      # Cap the export; remove for a full-collection dump.
      limit: 500000
      # Driver-side cursor batch size (network round-trip granularity).
      cursor_batch_size: 1000

  sink:
    type: parquet
    config:
      # Local filesystem destination. A path ending in `.parquet` writes a single
      # file; a directory path rolls over to `<uuid>.parquet` files instead.
      destination:
        type: local_path
        path: ./out/orders/
      # Codec applied to each column chunk: uncompressed | snappy | gzip | zstd | lz4.
      compression: zstd
      # Roll over to a new file every N rows (directory mode) to cap file size.
      max_rows_per_file: 200000
      # Rows per Arrow record batch handed to the writer. `0` = write whatever
      # the source hands over as one batch (recommended for Parquet, which
      # prefers fewer, larger row groups).
      batch_size: 0

## Orchestration (Airflow / Dagster + dbt)

[`orchestration/`](orchestration/) is a complete **ELT** recipe: load with
faucet, transform with dbt, schedule with Airflow or Dagster. faucet is
complementary to dbt — it owns Extract + Load (raw lossless rows into Postgres),
dbt owns Transform (typed, tested staging models), and because faucet is a single
binary the orchestrator just shells out to `faucet run`. See
[`orchestration/README.md`](orchestration/README.md) and the
[Orchestration cookbook page](../docs/book/src/cookbook/orchestration.md).

## Dashboards & alerts

The stack also provisions the shipped observability artifacts (issue #200):

```bash
docker compose -f examples/docker-compose.yml up -d prometheus grafana
```

Grafana at <http://localhost:3000> (admin / admin) pre-loads the four
`observability/grafana/` dashboards; Prometheus at <http://localhost:9095>
evaluates `observability/prometheus/alerts.yml` and scrapes a faucet process
on the host (enable the exporter with
`observability: { prometheus: { listen_addr: 0.0.0.0:9464 } }`).

## Covered by the local Docker stack

The service column lists what each example touches; all are provided by
`docker-compose.yml`. **S3** examples use MinIO — set the S3 endpoint to
`http://localhost:9000` with credentials `faucet` / `faucetfaucet`.

## Summary

Clears a batch of open **`good first issue`** items in one PR. Each is independent; grouped for a single review pass.

| Issue | Change |
|------|--------|
| #427 | `faucet list --json` — structured listing of sources/sinks/transforms/state stores (also `list --available --json`). |
| #428 | `faucet validate --json` — structured validation summary for CI (matrix **and** topology modes); prose report suppressed under `--json`. |
| #432 | `faucet schema --list` — enumerate the valid schema targets compiled into the binary. |
| #61  | Friendly snake-case `connector_name()` overrides for the **24 remaining** built-in connectors (matching the YAML `type:`), each with a specific-value test + a README observability note. |
| #430 | Fail-fast validation rejecting an empty `bucket` on the S3 / GCS sinks (typed `FaucetError::Config` at construction). |
| #431 | Actionable Kafka Schema-Registry encode errors — name the wire format and `schema_registry.url`. |
| #437 | Extract a pure, unit-tested `progress_ratio(done, planned)` in backfill metrics (0/0, over-count clamping). |
| #436 | Tests for the `RunStreamOptions` builder methods. |
| #435 | Boundary-case tests for the SFTP `glob_match` matcher (empty inputs, trailing `?`, over-long pattern). |
| #434 | Tests for `faucet init` `resolve_kinds` / `unknown_kind_err`. |
| #433 | Test for the `is_topology()` predicate. |
| #415 | Runnable `cli/examples/mongodb_to_parquet.yaml` (MongoDB → local Parquet) + `examples/README.md` mapping. |

## Notes

- **#61** deliberately changes `connector_name()` from the default stripped type name (e.g. `"CsvSource"`) to the friendly label (`"csv"`); the two registry tests that asserted the old default were updated accordingly. Two sinks (postgres, mysql) place their specific-value assertion in a testcontainer-gated conformance test (matching the pre-existing placement), so those two one-line methods are only exercised under Docker.
- **`--json` for `validate`** keeps the human report byte-identical when the flag is absent.
- Docs: `docs/book/src/reference/cli.md` documents all three new flags.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p faucet-core --lib` (RunStreamOptions builders), `-p faucet-cli --lib` (schema/list/init/topology/backfill/registry), `-p faucet-cli --test cli_end_to_end` (new `list --json` / `schema --list` / `validate --json` tests), `-p faucet-sink-kafka --features schema-registry` (encode messages), `-p faucet-sink-s3` / `-p faucet-sink-gcs` (bucket validation), `-p faucet-source-sftp` (glob).
- `cargo check --tests` across all 24 connector crates (conformance edits compile).
- `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p faucet-core --all-features` clean.

72:| `faucet-lineage` | `crates/lineage/` | OpenLineage event emission — HTTP/file/Kafka transports, schema facets, column-lineage analysis |
74:| `faucet-transform-wasm` | `crates/transform-wasm/` | WebAssembly transform (issue #124) — runs a user-provided precompiled `.wasm` module per record via `wasmtime` (lean embedding: `cranelift`+`runtime`+`std`, no component model/WASI). v1 ABI (`alloc`/`transform(ptr,len)->u64`/`memory`; optional `free`/`error_ptr`/`error_len`; packed return: `0`=drop, `u64::MAX`=error, else `(ptr<<32)|len`); host imports `faucet_v1::{log,now_ns}`. Sandbox: per-record fuel (CPU) + linear-memory cap (`StoreLimits` + `trap_on_grow_failure`). Compiled once, fresh `Store`+`Instance` per page (stateless across pages). `on_error: fail\|skip\|passthrough`. Compiles to a `TransformStage::PageFn` via `WasmTransform::into_page_stage`; `transform-wasm` feature |
75:| `faucet-stream` | `faucet-stream/` | Umbrella crate — feature-gated re-exports of all connectors and state backends |
76:| `faucet-cli` | `cli/` | `faucet` binary — YAML/JSON config-driven pipeline runner (`run`, `validate`, `schema`, `list`, `preview`, `init`, `doctor`, `test`, `schedule`, `serve`) |
78:## Architecture
92:- `transform.rs` — `RecordTransform` / `CompiledTransform`: built-ins — `flatten`, `rename_keys` (regex), `keys_case` (with `KeyCaseMode` — snake/camel/pascal/kebab/screaming_snake), `select`, `drop`, `set`, `rename_field`, `cast` (with `CastType` + `CastOnError`), `redact`, `value_case` (with `ValueCaseMode`), `spell_symbols` (with a built-in symbol → word map + optional `extra` overrides) — plus `Custom` closures. Built-in transforms are feature-gated (`transform-<name>`); the `transforms` aggregate enables all of them. The legacy `KeysToSnakeCase` / `transform-snake-case` was removed in favour of `KeysCase` — it was never relied on by external configs. `filter` and `explode` are stage-level transforms, not `RecordTransform` variants — see `stage.rs`. **`sql`** is a page-level transform (`TransformStage::PageFn`) backed by embedded DuckDB (`faucet-transform-sql` crate, `transform-sql` feature). Each page is registered as the `batch` relation; the query result replaces the page. CI is running (~25 min); a monitor will alert me on any failure or completion, and auto-merge lands it the moment the required checks pass.

## What shipped (one PR)

**CLI features** (code + tests + `docs/book/src/reference/cli.md`)
- **#427** `faucet list --json` (+ `list --available --json`)
- **#428** `faucet validate --json` — structured summary for matrix *and* topology modes; prose report unchanged without the flag
- **#432** `faucet schema --list` — enumerates valid targets

**#61** — friendly `connector_name()` on the **24 remaining** built-in connectors (delegated to two parallel agents), each with a specific-value test + README note. Two pre-existing registry tests that asserted the old `"CsvSource"`/`"StdoutSink"` defaults were updated to the new labels.

**Reliability / validation**
- **#430** empty-`bucket` rejection on S3/GCS sinks (typed error at construction)
- **#431** actionable Kafka Schema-Registry encode errors (name the format + `schema_registry.url`)
- **#437** pure, unit-tested `progress_ratio` in backfill metrics

**Test hardening** — **#436** `RunStreamOptions` builders, **#435** SFTP `glob_match` boundaries, **#434** `init` `resolve_kinds`, **#433** `is_topology`

**#415** — runnable `mongodb_to_parquet.yaml` + `examples/README` mapping (validates clean)

**#438** — synced the crate table (added 30 missing rows) and counts (64→92) in `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/rules/architecture.md`. Note these files are **gitignored in this repo**, so per your call I edited them locally; they won't appear in the PR.

## Verification done locally
- `faucet-core` (RunStreamOptions tests), `faucet-cli` lib (867 pass) + `cli_end_to_end` (my 3 new `--json`/`--list` tests pass), `faucet-sink-kafka` encode (11 pass), s3/gcs/sftp lib tests, `cargo check --tests` across all 24 connector crates, `cargo fmt --check` clean, clippy clean on core + the logic-changed crates and my CLI code (the 8 clippy warnings I saw were pre-existing feature-gated vars in files I didn't touch, absent under CI's `--all-features`).

Two caveats I'm relying on CI (`--all-features`) to confirm, since I can't link all-features locally (disk): the feature-gated `validate.rs` cfg blocks (schedule/notify/lineage — trivial guard edits) and the postgres/mysql **sink** `connector_name` assertions (their conformance tests are Docker-gated, matching prior placement). I'll fix anything CI flags and keep it armed until it's green and merged.

One aside: there are two stray untracked files in your working tree (`cli/x`, `.entire/`) that I deliberately kept out of the commit. Want me to remove them, or leave them?
